releaseNotes: 10.20.0: two-factor by an authenticator app. Minor bump, opt-in: a host that does not call AddSolhigsonTwoFactor sees no two-factor change, and its sign-in answers as in 10.19.0. Registration (Solhigson.Framework.Identity): identityBuilder.AddSolhigsonTwoFactor(configure), on the IdentityBuilder AddSolhigsonIdentityManager returns, registers TwoFactorManager scoped; replaces Identity's EF UserStore with RootEncryptingUserStore, which stores the authenticator key as a root-encrypted rk1: envelope, so the host also calls AddRootEncryption in the same release, never after it: without the ring every enrolment answers NeedsRootRing, and a stored key's read throws InvalidOperationException, so a right password for an enabled enrolled account throws out of SignInAsync whatever Enabled says and DisableAsync answers Failed; adds AuthenticatorKeysRootStore to the ring census and re-encryption; registers the counter store and TwoFactorOptions (Issuer, required; Enabled and RequiredForGroupsEnabled, Func<IServiceProvider, bool> switches on when unset; RequiredForGroups, role-group names compared ordinally, empty unless set, and empty no account must enrol; CodeCapFailsClosed, false unless set); and turns on the identity manager's second factor for the builder's user type. AddSolhigsonRootEncryptedAuthenticatorKeys registers the store and the census entry alone. A host fails at start when Issuer is blank, IdentityOptions.Lockout.MaxFailedAccessAttempts is below 2 or DefaultLockoutTimeSpan is not above zero. TwoFactorManager answers a TwoFactorResult (Outcome, a TwoFactorOutcome; EndSessions, NotifyHolder and HadPassword for the app's flow and audit; SharedSecret and AuthenticatorUriSecret for an enrolment): BeginEnrolmentAsync, CurrentEnrolmentAsync and CompleteEnrolmentAsync enrol; DisableAsync turns two-factor off only with a live code; ResetAsync(user, actingUserId) is an administrator's removal of another user's factor and password together, a self-reset refused (NotOwn); RequiresEnrolmentAsync answers whether an account in a RequiredForGroups role group must enrol, for the app's gate. Sign-in: SignInAsync answers an enrolled account RequiresTwoFactor with SignInResponse.PendingUserId, and SolhigsonIdentityManager.TwoFactorSignInAsync(code, pendingUserId) is the code step; SignInOutcome gains AuthenticatorUnreadable, TwoFactorTimedOut, TooManyCodeAttempts and CodeCapUnavailable, and SignInResponse gains PendingUserId and NotifyHolder. While Enabled is off an enrolled account signs in on its password alone, with one Warning. Code attempts at sign-in and at a disable share one cap per account, MaxFailedAccessAttempts per DefaultLockoutTimeSpan window, counted before the code is checked; a wrong code counts toward lockout, and the first code lockout of a streak lasts DefaultLockoutTimeSpan and each later one twice the last, up to 24 hours (TwoFactorLockout.EscalatedLockout), a streak living 30 days from its last lockout. A stored key the ring cannot open (not-an-envelope, not-in-ring, malformed, failed-authentication) reads as no key with one Error under Solhigson.Framework.Identity.AuthenticatorKey (AuthenticatorKeyStorage), and the framework's sign-in refuses its account (AuthenticatorUnreadable). Meter Solhigson.Framework.Identity: password_sign_in gains the step tag (password, code) beside outcome, and two_factor counts each TwoFactorManager call but RequiresEnrolmentAsync, tagged method and outcome; TwoFactorManager's lines are under Solhigson.Framework.Identity.TwoFactor (TwoFactorDiagnostics), a disable's wrong-code counting and lockout lines and the counter clearing after a disable or a reset under Solhigson.Framework.Identity. Counter store (Solhigson.Framework.Throttling): ICounterStore (CountAsync, ResetAsync; CounterResult, CounterExpiry) counts per key atomically and answers Unavailable when it cannot; RedisCounterStore, registered once by AddSolhigsonThrottling or AddSolhigsonTwoFactor, needs an IConnectionMultiplexer and a Redis run with maxmemory-policy noeviction, and never falls back to memory; UseInMemoryCounterStore() replaces it with InMemoryCounterStore, per process, for a single host. While the store cannot count, code attempts are counted per process (refused, with CodeCapFailsClosed on) and code lockouts do not escalate, Identity's own lockout standing. A disable or a reset whose lost commit is read back as landed answers Disabled or Reset and leaves the account object detached, so after a Disabled or Reset answer the app reloads the account (UserManager.FindByIdAsync) before writing it again in the request: UserManager.UpdateAsync of the detached object throws EF's InvalidOperationException with Identity's default user validator. Where another request saved the account after the commit, the object keeps this call's concurrency stamp, so UserManager.UpdateAsync without a validator answers ConcurrencyFailure and a context's Update then SaveChangesAsync throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException and writes nothing, and one Warning names the account's id and the method. RequiresEnrolmentAsync never empties its cached entry for an account no longer stored: it answers false and leaves the entry as it was. Changed without opting in: a declared Secret setting's table read is answered from the settings cache, in the process's memory only, until a save, a reset or a delete of any setting made through the framework evicts every cached setting on every instance, while a write made around it is seen when the entry expires (a day by default), and a declared table setting absent with no Default is cached as absent; GetUserDetailsByIdAsync, GetUserDetailsByUsernameAsync and GetUserDetailsByEmailAsync read each role with its group in one cached query, evicted by a saved change to a role or a role group, and no longer write the group onto the role instance the cache holds; password_sign_in carries step password on every host; AddSolhigsonThrottling also registers the Redis ICounterStore, which the identity manager's constructor takes, so a hand-built container that builds the manager registers an IHostEnvironment with an application name, or its own store; the throttle's outage Error names the fault's type, never the driver's message. The identity manager's three public constructors gain optional IOptions<TwoFactorOptions>, ICounterStore and IServiceProvider parameters: source compatible, but an assembly compiled against an earlier Core that constructs the manager, directly or from a derived class, throws MissingMethodException until rebuilt. A consumer's own type named as one Solhigson.Framework.Identity gains (TwoFactorManager, TwoFactorResult, TwoFactorOutcome, TwoFactorDiagnostics, TwoFactorOptions, TwoFactorIdentityBuilderExtensions, TwoFactorLockout, RootEncryptingUserStore, AuthenticatorKeyStorage, AuthenticatorKeysRootStore) or Solhigson.Framework.Throttling gains (ICounterStore, CounterResult, CounterExpiry, RedisCounterStore, InMemoryCounterStore), brought into a file by a using directive alongside that framework namespace, is ambiguous there (CS0104) until the local copy is deleted or the use qualified. A consumer adopting two-factor follows the steps in RELEASING.md. 10.19.0: sign-in hardening and the breached-password check. Minor bump. SolhigsonIdentityManager.SignInAsync (Solhigson.Framework.Identity) does one password-hash verification whatever the account's state, while that state does not change during the call: where Identity answers without hashing it verifies against a fixed hash (SignInFixedHash, a singleton AddSolhigsonIdentityManager registers), the password hasher given null for an unknown name. SignInResponse gains Outcome (SignInOutcome: Succeeded, RequiresTwoFactor, LockedOut, Rejected, Disabled) and LockedByThisAttempt; every call counts on the new meter Solhigson.Framework.Identity (password_sign_in, tagged outcome), and the attempt that locks an account writes a Warning naming its id. UnlockAsync(userName) clears an account's lockout end and failed count in one write and writes an Information line. Tightened without opting in: lockOutOnFailure defaults to true, so a caller that omits it counts failures toward lockout once rebuilt; an account whose Enabled is false is refused even with the right password (Outcome Disabled, User null, no cookie, no second factor asked); a right password whose account cannot be read back is signed out. The three public constructors gain optional SignInFixedHash and ILoggerFactory parameters: source compatible, but an assembly compiled against an earlier Core that constructs the manager, directly or from a derived class, throws MissingMethodException until rebuilt. Breach check, opt-in: identityBuilder.AddSolhigsonBreachedPasswordCheck(configure) registers BreachedPasswordCheck (Breached, Clear or Unchecked), BreachedPasswordValidator for the builder's user type and BreachedPasswordRangeCache; only the first five hex characters of the password's SHA-1 are sent, to api.pwnedpasswords.com, the range is cached an hour by that prefix, and no hash or verdict is stored; a failure answers Unchecked with one Error (the check fails open), and five in a row pause the calls for a minute. A consumer's own type named as one Solhigson.Framework.Identity gains (SignInOutcome, SignInDiagnostics, SignInFixedHash, BreachedPasswordCheck, BreachedPasswordOptions, BreachedPasswordRangeCache, BreachedPasswordResult, BreachedPasswordValidator, BreachedPasswordIdentityBuilderExtensions), brought into a file by a using directive alongside that framework namespace, is ambiguous there (CS0104) until the local copy is deleted or the use qualified. A consumer passes lockOutOnFailure: false only on purpose, reads Outcome where it read User.Enabled after a sign-in, rebuilds an assembly that constructs the manager, and, adopting the breach check, maps its own switch onto BreachedPasswordOptions.Enabled, which is on when unset; the full steps are in RELEASING.md. 10.18.0: the OTLP log export, the API-exchange masker and export, and the Loki readers. Minor bump, every piece opt-in: a host that calls none of AddSolhigsonLogExport, UseSolhigsonLogScope and AddSolhigsonLokiReader sees no logging change but the job runs below. Restore: every consumer now receives OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol and OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting 1.15.3 with their transitive packages; one referencing any of them below 1.15.3 raises it to 1.15.3 or later, adopting or not, or restore fails with NU1605, and one restoring in locked mode regenerates its lock files. Export (Solhigson.Framework.Logging.Export): AddSolhigsonLogExport, called after any ClearProviders(), adds the OpenTelemetry logging provider beside NLog; logs export only when Solhigson:Logs:OtlpExportEnabled is true and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set (OtlpExportState). The endpoint is https unless loopback: with any OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*HEADERS key set, an endpoint that is neither turns the export off, but with none set it is not enforced, and a plain-http endpoint carries personal data in clear. Traces and metrics join through SolhigsonLogExportOptions.OpenTelemetry and export only while logs export. Every call ignores inbound trace context, in the DI DistributedContextPropagator and the SDK's process-wide default propagator. While exporting, ScopedPropertiesLogProcessor adds chainId, the ExportedLogProperties, client.address and enduser.id, and replaces the request's raw path in a line by its route template; UseSolhigsonLogScope(), before UseRouting, opens the request's log scope. Nothing else is rewritten or redacted: every template property, the formatted message, and an exception's type, message and stack trace export as written (a URL's query keeps its values), and the path rewrite misses an exception's text, a path after a schemeless host, a byte[] attribute, a multi-dimensional array attribute (which leaves the record's other attributes unrewritten too), a path followed by a percent-encoded / or ., and one preceded by ./ or ../. Every line then goes to an off-host store, so a host audits what its lines write before turning the switch on. Spans keep raw paths. Masker (Solhigson.Framework.Web.Api): ApiTraceMasker under ApiTraceMaskOptions, whose ProtectedFields always hold ProtectedFieldsFloor. API exchanges: with Solhigson:Logs:ApiLogsToLokiEnabled also true, LokiApiTraceSink exports each masked exchange as the service <app>.ApiLogs, carrying enduser_id, counted on the meter Solhigson.Framework.LogExport; the LoggingApiTraceSink line is then not written. Readers (Solhigson.Framework.Logging.Loki): AddSolhigsonLokiReader registers IAppLogReader and IApiLogReader, which read while Solhigson:Logs:LokiReadEnabled is true from Solhigson:Logs:LokiUrl, LokiUser and LokiToken, and check no permission. Changed without opting in: a job a framework Hangfire server runs gets its own root activity (JobRunEnvelopeFilter.ActivitySourceName) and log property scope, its trace id the chain id; with no tracer on that source, an outbound call it makes carries a sampled traceparent. A consumer's own type named as one Solhigson.Framework.Logging.Export gains (ApiLogExportPipeline, LogExportDiagnostics, LogPropertyScopeMiddleware, LokiApiTraceSink, OtlpExportOffReason, OtlpExportState, ScopedPropertiesLogProcessor, SolhigsonLogExportOptions, SolhigsonLogExportServiceCollectionExtensions, SolhigsonLogScopeApplicationBuilderExtensions), Solhigson.Framework.Logging.Loki gains (ApiLogRecord, ApiLogSearchRequest, AppLogNewestRecord, AppLogRecord, AppLogSearchRequest, CursorPagedList, IApiLogReader, IAppLogReader, LokiApiLogReader, LokiAppLogReader, LokiReadClient, SolhigsonLokiReaderOptions, SolhigsonLokiReaderServiceCollectionExtensions) or Solhigson.Framework.Web.Api gains (ApiTraceMasker, ApiTraceMaskOptions), brought into a file by a using directive alongside that framework namespace, is ambiguous there (CS0104) until the local copy is deleted or the use qualified; in a namespace that declares its own type of that name, the local one wins with no error and the framework's is qualified. 10.17.0: permission groups, opt-in, and the multi-role menu fix. Minor bump: every permission-group behaviour waits for AddPermissionGroups, so a host that does not call it sees no permission-group change. Declaring (Solhigson.Framework.Identity): [AllowedGroups(...)] on a public string permission constant, or AllowedGroups on a [PermissionInfo] class attribute or a subclass of it such as [PermissionInfoMenuRoot] (Solhigson.Framework.Web.Attributes), names the role groups whose roles may hold the permission; PermissionGroupDeclarations.ReadFrom(permissionsType, knownGroups) reads them into one map (Names, KnownGroups, Allows, TryGetGroups, GroupsOf, IsKnownGroup) and leaves a name with no declaration, no group, an unknown group or a shared name closed to every group, listed in Problems (PermissionGroupDeclarationProblem; PermissionGroupDeclarationFault NoDeclaration, NoGroup, UnknownGroup or SharedName, a SharedName being a name held at two declaring sites, or spellings differing only in letter case or trailing whitespace). services.AddPermissionGroups(typeof(<permission constants>), <group names>, options) (Solhigson.Framework.Web.Authorization.PermissionGroupServiceCollectionExtensions) registers that map as a singleton, PermissionGroupOptions, and PermissionGroupReconciler scoped as an open generic, and throws on a second call. Checking: with groups registered, PermissionManager.VerifyPermissionAsync, after its stored-grant check, refuses an undeclared permission whatever the switch, passes a holding role in a group the permission declares, and on any other mismatch reads PermissionGroupOptions.Enforce (a Func<IServiceProvider, bool>, off when absent): on refuses, off passes with a Warning; a switch that throws refuses and writes one Error. Each mismatch writes a once-per-host Warning per role, permission and outcome (PermissionGroupOutcome) and is counted on the meter Solhigson.Framework.PermissionGroups (permission_group_mismatch); every line is under the logger category Solhigson.Framework.PermissionGroups and starts "Permission group:" (PermissionGroupDiagnostics). A role's menu (GetMenuPermissionsForRoleCachedAsync) and listing (GetAllPermissionsForRoleCached) leave out an undeclared permission and, with enforcement on, one the role's group may not hold. A menu root is a permission: undeclared, it and all its children are left out of every role's menu whatever the switch, and the reconcile skips its grants with no line; a root is declared on the permissions type passed, by AllowedGroups on its [PermissionInfoMenuRoot] there or, when there is none, by an [AllowedGroups] constant of its name (both for one name is a SharedName). VerifyPermissionAsync(string, ClaimsPrincipal, CancellationToken) is a new overload. Granting (PermissionManager, no switch read): GetOfferedPermissionsForRoleAsync lists the stored permissions the role's group may hold, each with whether the role holds it (OfferedPermissionDto); SetRolePermissionsAsync adds and removes grants among those only, in one tracked save, leaves every grant it did not offer, and returns each dropped id with its reason (DroppedPermissionDto, PermissionGrantDropReason); GetAllowedGroupsAsync lists each permission's declared groups (PermissionAllowedGroupsDto); without groups the editor offers every permission. With groups registered, GiveAccessToRoleAsync refuses an out-of-group or undeclared permission and stores nothing, and discovery's AllowedRoles seeding, which goes through it, writes one Warning per refused role and name. Start-up: with groups registered, DiscoverNewPermissionsAsync writes one Information line (the declared count, the known groups and what the switch reads) and one Error per declaration problem, per undeclared [Permission] name on a controller or action and per blank name, never throwing for them and never changing discovery's result. Role groups: with groups registered, RoleGroupManager.AddRoleToGroupAsync refuses to move a role that holds a grant into another group and RoleGroupManager.UpdateAsync refuses to rename a group any of whose roles holds one, each writing a Warning and throwing InvalidOperationException, changing nothing; RoleManager<TRole>.UpdateAsync writing a role's RoleGroupId, and any write to RoleGroupId through the context, are not checked. Reconciling: PermissionGroupReconciler<TUser, TRole, TContext, TKey>.RunAsync(strip, cancellationToken) names each stored grant outside its permission's declared groups in a Warning of its own and, with strip true, re-reads and re-judges each and removes it by a tracked delete with its own save; a stale grant (no role, no group, an unknown group, no permission, or an undeclared permission) is kept and listed, the first 100 named in a Warning each and the rest counted in one line; an undeclared menu root's grant is skipped and counted (MenuRootsSkipped); the PermissionGroupReconcileResult lists each outside and stale grant (PermissionGroupReconcileRow, PermissionGroupGrantClass, PermissionGroupStaleReason, PermissionGroupReconcileAction) with the counts. A strip is audited only when the host includes SolhigsonRolePermission<TKey> in its AuditCaptureRegistry (an instance call on the registered singleton), its identity context carries AuditCaptureSaveChangesInterceptor and maps AuditTrail, and, with AuditCaptureOptions.RequireAttributedActor on, the run has an attributed user; otherwise the reconcile's Warning lines and result rows are its only record. Changed without opting in: GetMenuPermissionsForRoleCachedAsync for a user with several roles merged their menus into one role's cached menu objects, and building more than one role's menu in one request scope could carry one role's child into another role's cached menu through a menu parent both builds loaded, so a user with one role could be shown another role's menu items until the cache expired (no page access was granted); each role's cached menu now stays its own. HangfireTypes judges a refused type name by whole code points: a lone surrogate or a hidden supplementary code point (a tag character) now shows as one '?' in its log line and exception, while other BMP text is unchanged. PermissionManager's constructor gains optional PermissionGroupDeclarations, IOptions<PermissionGroupOptions>, IServiceProvider and ILoggerFactory parameters and RoleGroupManager's optional PermissionGroupDeclarations and ILoggerFactory ones: source compatible, but the old two-parameter and one-parameter constructors are gone, so an assembly compiled against an earlier Core that calls them, directly or from a derived class, throws MissingMethodException until rebuilt; a class deriving from either manager forwards the new parameters to its base, or permission groups stay off in it. A consumer's own type named as one Solhigson.Framework.Identity gains (AllowedGroupsAttribute, PermissionGroupDeclarations, PermissionGroupDeclarationProblem, PermissionGroupDeclarationFault, PermissionGroupOutcome, PermissionGroupDiagnostics, PermissionGroupOptions, PermissionGroupReconciler, PermissionGroupReconcileResult, PermissionGroupReconcileRow, PermissionGroupGrantClass, PermissionGroupStaleReason, PermissionGroupReconcileAction), Solhigson.Framework.Dto gains (OfferedPermissionDto, DroppedPermissionDto, PermissionGrantDropReason, PermissionAllowedGroupsDto) or Solhigson.Framework.Web.Authorization gains (PermissionGroupServiceCollectionExtensions), brought into a file by a using directive alongside that framework namespace, is ambiguous there (CS0104) until the local copy is deleted or the use qualified; in a namespace that declares its own type of that name, the local one wins with no error and the framework's is qualified, so a host's own AllowedGroupsAttribute beside its permission constants leaves each constant it marks undeclared (a NoDeclaration Error at start, and refused) until it is deleted. 10.16.0: the settings declaration and the root ring. In Solhigson.Framework.Infrastructure.ApplicationSettings, [SettingsGroup] names an AppSettingsBase type's group and [Setting] declares a property (Purpose, Source Startup, File or Table, Reason, Default, Floor, Ceiling, Sensitivity None, Personal or Secret), read by its own name through AppSettingsBase's Read<T> and ReadList; SettingsCatalog.Of builds the catalog from the group types and refuses a malformed declaration, SettingsCatalog.Report gives the declarations as startup-report lines, and SolhigsonConfigurationService.UseSettingsCatalog registers the catalog, after which CreateApplicationSettingAsync and UpdateApplicationSettingAsync hold a row to its declaration (SettingsCatalog.Refusal). SolhigsonConfigurationService.ListDeclaredSettingsAsync returns a DeclaredSettingsListing: each declared setting with the value in force and its origin, and each row that breaks a declaration. In Solhigson.Framework.Security, SecretSettingName (IsMatch, TryMatch, Classify) classifies secret setting names; services.AddRootEncryption(configuration) registers the AES-256-GCM root ring (IRootEncryptor, RootEncryptor, RootEnvelope) and RootSettingEncryptor as the setting encryptor, and RootReEncryption over each IRootEncryptedStore (AppSettingsRootStore for the settings table) gives CensusAsync, the values under each key id, the unreadable ones with their reason and the plain rows with secret-looking names, and ReEncryptAsync, which moves each readable value to the current key and reports each run to an optional IRootReEncryptionRunObserver as a RootReEncryptionRun; SettingsRead.DecryptFailed marks a table read whose sensitive row's decrypt threw a CryptographicException. Lifts: ConcurrencyRetry.ExecuteWithConcurrencyRetryAsync (Solhigson.Framework.EfCore), a bounded optimistic-concurrency retry whose delegate contract obliges the delegate to detach every entry an earlier attempt loaded, changed, added or removed, never Clear(); HangfirePassLock with IPassLock and IPassLease (Solhigson.Framework.Jobs), which JobRunStore.TryAcquireLock now uses; BoundedBody.ReadAsync (Solhigson.Framework.Web), a bounded request-body read whose TooLarge outcome answers 413. Tightened: a save landing sensitive with no encryptor or a LegacySettingEncryptor registered is refused, naming AddRootEncryption; a plain save of an undeclared row, or of a declared Secret, whose name SecretSettingName.Classify refuses is refused, while a declared non-Secret setting's name is judged at compile time by SOLT007 alone; a host that calls AddRootEncryption reads no row written under LegacySettingEncryptor and RootReEncryption cannot convert one (the ring census, which runs only with the ring registered, names it LegacyUnreadable), so each such secret, whose old key ships in this package, is rotated at its issuer before the switch and its new value saved after it. Also changed: GetApplicationSettingAsync returns an untracked instance, so an edit to it persists only through UpdateApplicationSettingAsync, which writes Value and IsSensitive only; Create and Update refuse while another setting has unsaved edits in the scope; ConfigurationWrapper warnings and errors logged before the logger factory existed are now written. A consumer's own type named ConcurrencyRetry, BoundedBody, BoundedBodyOutcome, HangfirePassLock, IPassLock or IPassLease, or one of the names Solhigson.Framework.Infrastructure.ApplicationSettings gains (SettingAttribute, SettingsGroupAttribute, SettingSource, SettingSensitivity, SettingsCatalog, SettingsCatalogEntry, DeclaredSettingsListing, DeclaredSettingLine, UndeclaredSettingRow, SettingFlag, SettingFlagKind, SettingValueOrigin, SettingEncryptorKind) or Solhigson.Framework.Security gains (SecretSettingName, SecretSettingClassification, SecretSettingOutcome, IRootEncryptor, RootEncryptor, RootEnvelope, RootEncryptionRegistration, RootSettingEncryptor, IRootEncryptedStore, AppSettingsRootStore, RootReEncryption, RootEncryptionCensus, IRootReEncryptionRunObserver, RootReEncryptionRun and their result types), brought into a file by a using directive alongside the framework namespace, is ambiguous there (CS0104) until the local copy is deleted or the use qualified; in a namespace that declares its own type of that name, the framework's is qualified.
